show: A Christmas Carol - Il Musical by Compagnia BIT (Italian original musical, original music and lyrics by Stefano Lori and Marco Caselle, book and direction by Melina Pellicano)
synopsis:
On Christmas Eve in London, Ebenezer Scrooge sits alone at his counting-house, guarding his money and rejecting every gesture of warmth around him. He treats his clerk, Bob Cratchit, with harsh economy, dismisses his nephew Fred’s invitation to Christmas dinner, and turns away those seeking help for people in need. That night, the dead Jacob Marley appears before him, burdened by the chains he forged through a life of selfishness. Marley warns Scrooge that he still has a chance to escape the same fate, but only if he listens to three Spirits who will visit before morning.

The Ghost of Christmas Past carries Scrooge back through his own memories. He sees the lonely schoolboy he once was; his beloved younger sister Fan, arriving with news that he may come home; and the exuberant Christmas celebration held by his first employer, Mr. Fezziwig. These scenes reveal the affection, joy, and human connection Scrooge gradually abandoned. The Ghost of Christmas Present then takes him into the homes of others, including the Cratchits, where Bob, his wife Rose, and their children make a loving Christmas meal despite their poverty. Scrooge is moved by the fragile kindness and courage of Tiny Tim.

Finally, the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come shows a bleak future shaped by Scrooge’s unaltered life: strangers speak indifferently of a dead man, his possessions are taken away, and his grave stands lonely and unlamented. Horrified, Scrooge begs for the chance to change. He awakens on Christmas morning transformed, sends a generous gift to the Cratchits, joins Fred’s celebration, and begins to treat Bob and Tiny Tim with genuine care.

The musical explores how isolation and greed can harden a person, but also how remembrance, empathy, and moral courage can restore them. Its central message is that generosity and love become meaningful through action, especially toward people who need them most.

show: Alice nel Paese delle Meraviglie - Il Musical, the Italian-produced original musical touring Italian theatres (not the Disney film version)
synopsis:
Alice is a thirteen-year-old girl who is weary of being told that it is time to grow up and decide what she will become. Longing to stop the clock and escape the demands closing in around her, she follows the White Rabbit down his burrow and enters Wonderland, a place where ordinary rules no longer apply. There she is swept through a succession of startling transformations and encounters: doors refuse to behave as expected, animals speak with absolute confidence, and every new path seems to overturn the logic of the last. Guided, teased, and perplexed by the Caterpillar, the Cheshire Cat, and the March Hare, Alice tries to understand the strange world while also trying to understand herself. At the Mad Hatter’s gathering, time seems to have become as unruly as the people around the table, turning conversation and celebration into a whirl of riddles and confusion.

As Alice ventures further into Wonderland, the atmosphere darkens under the rule of the Queen of Hearts, whose court is obsessed with obedience, playing cards, and the threat of punishment. The Queen’s explosive temper makes even the smallest mistake dangerous, while the King, the court, and the card soldiers reinforce a world in which nonsense is treated as law. Alice is drawn into the Queen’s proceedings and ultimately faces a trial where accusations, verdicts, and rules shift without warning. Refusing to be intimidated any longer, she challenges the authority of the court and the fear that has governed her journey. As the chaotic figures of Wonderland close around her, Alice’s resolve allows her to confront the nightmare rather than submit to it, bringing her extraordinary adventure to its decisive conclusion.

The musical explores growing up as a confusing passage between childhood freedom and adult expectations. Through Alice’s journey, it celebrates curiosity, courage, and the discovery that power loses much of its hold when fear is faced directly.

show: Aggiungi un posto a tavola, the Italian musical comedy by Garinei & Giovannini with music by Armando Trovajoli, premiered 1974
synopsis:
In a small mountain village, the warm-hearted parish priest Don Silvestro is rehearsing a community musical when he receives an extraordinary telephone call: God tells him that a new flood is coming and commands him to build an ark for the entire village. Though bewildered, Don Silvestro accepts the task and rallies the villagers to construct the vessel before the appointed day. His work is complicated by Crispino, the miserly Mayor, who resents the priest and repeatedly tries to thwart the project; by Crispino’s daughter Clementina, whose intense love for Don Silvestro tests his vocation; and by Consolazione, a glamorous woman sent to distract the village men from their labour. Her arrival causes jealous uproar among the wives, but it also changes the life of Totò, the innocent village simpleton. Totò falls sincerely in love with Consolazione, and his devotion gradually allows her to imagine a life beyond the role others have assigned her.

Against the obstacles, the ark is completed. Yet, just as the flood is due, a Cardinal arrives from Rome and persuades the frightened villagers that Don Silvestro has dishonoured his priesthood and cannot be trusted. Abandoned by those he has struggled to save, Don Silvestro boards the ark with only Clementina beside him. When the waters begin to rise around the villagers, however, he refuses the safety reserved for him. He leaves the ark to stand with his people, choosing solidarity over personal survival. Moved by this act, God stops the flood and restores calm to the village. The danger passes, divisions soften, and the community gathers at a long, welcoming table where every person has a place.

The musical celebrates generosity, forgiveness, and the courage to include those whom a community has judged or excluded. Its central image of making room at the table turns fellowship into an answer to fear, selfishness, and division.

show: Belle e la Bestia - Il Musical by Compagnia dell'ORA, the Italian original musical with its own original score (not the Disney Beauty and the Beast)
synopsis:
In a distant castle, a young Prince is punished for his arrogance and imprisoned in the body of a Beast. The curse blurs his memories, leaving only fragments of a life before—above all, the fading image of a Princess and a love seemingly lost beyond time. The spell can be broken only by a person capable of loving him with complete sincerity, even at the cost of her own life. Meanwhile, Belle, a young woman of pure heart and free spirit, is drawn by chance into the Beast’s isolated world. Her arrival awakens something long dormant in him: a tender, elusive stirring of feeling, and the memory of the princess’s face that the spell had erased for ever.

As Belle and the Beast come to know one another, their relationship moves beyond fear and appearances. Within the enchanted castle, mystery, humour, and magic accompany Belle’s growing understanding of the wounded man concealed by the Beast’s frightening exterior. Yet their chance of happiness is threatened by Miguel, Belle’s forceful and unreturned suitor. Determined to possess her at any price, Miguel schemes to make Belle his wife, driven by jealousy and ambition rather than love. His deception intensifies the danger surrounding Belle and places the fragile bond between her and the Beast under severe strain.

The Beast must confront the cruelty and pride that caused his downfall, while Belle must decide whether she can trust what she sees in his heart rather than what appears before her. As buried memories begin to surface, the question becomes urgent: can what grows between them overturn the curse before Miguel’s designs destroy them both? The answer rests not in magic alone, but in a choice to love freely, bravely, and without possession.

The musical explores how inner character matters more than outward form, and how humility can transform a life damaged by pride. It also contrasts genuine, selfless love with jealousy, control, and the desire to possess another person.

show: C'era una volta... Scugnizzi, the Italian musical by Claudio Mattone (2001), staged at Teatro Sistina in Rome
synopsis:
In Naples, two former inmates of the Nisida juvenile detention centre emerge into adulthood having chosen radically different paths. Saverio De Lucia becomes Don Saverio, a street priest who works among the city’s neglected young people—its scugnizzi, children growing up amid poverty, vulnerability, and the pull of the streets. Through volunteering and music, he tries to give them discipline, belonging, and the belief that their lives can be directed by something other than fear or necessity. Among the young people in his care are Rosa and Carmine, whose circumstances make them especially susceptible to the promises of easy money and protection.

Saverio’s old fellow inmate, Raffaele Capasso—known as ’o Russo—has taken the opposite route. He is now a Camorra boss, ruling through intimidation and using local children as couriers in his criminal operations. Where Don Saverio sees young people with talent and a future worth defending, ’o Russo sees obedient recruits and disposable tools. Their reunion turns their shared past into a bitter present-day conflict: each man understands the world the boys and girls inhabit, but each offers them a wholly different way to survive it.

As Don Saverio’s influence grows, the youngsters begin to discover confidence in one another and in music, threatening ’o Russo’s control. The criminal boss becomes increasingly enraged by the priest’s refusal to yield and by the children’s growing resistance. The confrontation culminates in tragedy when ’o Russo kills Don Saverio. Yet the murder does not secure his victory. Shaken by the loss of the man who trusted them, the scugnizzi reject the criminal authority that has shaped their lives and turn their grief into an open, defiant cry against the Camorra.

The musical is about the collision between solidarity and exploitation, hope and resignation, music and violence. It argues that even after devastating loss, collective courage can break the silence imposed by criminal power.

show: Forza Venite Gente, the 1981 Italian musical about Saint Francis of Assisi
synopsis:
In Assisi, the young Francis Bernardone is the admired, carefree son of Pietro Bernardone, a prosperous cloth merchant who expects him to inherit both his business and his worldly ambitions. Yet Francis begins to turn away from the life his father has planned. His growing spiritual longing, hinted at in private encounters with a mysterious blond angel, leads him to reject wealth publicly, exchange fine clothes for a rough habit, and embrace a life among the poor. Pietro, bewildered and furious, cannot understand why his son would abandon security, family standing, and material success for an existence of voluntary poverty.

As Francis gathers companions, he teaches them to trust Providence, to live simply, and to meet hardship with joy. His former friends struggle with his transformation, while Pietro and the Cenciosa punctuate the action with commentary that ranges from comic disbelief to personal grief. Francis and his brothers travel to Rome to seek Pope Innocent III’s approval for their way of life; elsewhere, Francis preaches to birds and reconciles the people of Gubbio with the wolf that has terrorised their town. Clare is drawn to Francis’s vision and renounces her privileged life, but she must confront the painful difference between personal love and the wider love to which Francis feels called.

Francis’s journey carries him to the Holy Land amid the violence of the Crusades, where a knight and a Muslim voice a shared yearning for peace. Back in Italy, he creates the Nativity scene at Greccio, confronts the Devil’s temptations, and explains to Brother Leo that “perfect joy” lies not in success or comfort but in accepting rejection and suffering without losing love. As illness overtakes him, Francis faces Sister Death serenely. After his death, Assisi mourns, and the company closes in praise of creation.

The musical explores the cost of choosing conscience over comfort, especially within the painful bond between father and son. It celebrates poverty, compassion, peace, kinship with the natural world, and the possibility of finding joy even in suffering.

show: FRIDA Opera Musical by MIC International Company, written by Andrea Ortis and Gianmario Pagano, directed by Andrea Ortis
synopsis:
La Catrina steps forward as Frida Kahlo’s guide, inviting the audience into a Mexico where colour, ritual, satire, and death move side by side with the living. Around her, post-revolutionary Mexico erupts with political idealism, mural art, European avant-gardes, and the restless presence of figures such as Zapata, Trotsky, Breton, and Tina Modotti. Within this turbulent world, Frida confronts a body marked by pain and turns suffering into an unyielding will to live, paint, and define herself on her own terms.

Her relationship with Diego Rivera becomes the story’s fierce emotional centre. Their bond is immense and combustible: a meeting of artistic ambition, political conviction, erotic attraction, mutual support, and repeated conflict. Love joins them, but betrayals and infidelities wound them; their shared public life amplifies both their successes and their private fractures. Rather than offering escape, their relationship forces Frida to face the cost of devotion, independence, and artistic honesty.

La Catrina accompanies these passages as an intermediary between the earthly and the symbolic, framing Frida’s experiences within a Mexico in which life and death continually dance together. As Frida moves through physical anguish, emotional upheaval, and a changing nation, art becomes her means of resistance: pain is transformed into colour, vulnerability into creative force, and personal rebellion into a demand for freedom. The action gathers Frida, Diego, their circle, and the broader Mexican landscape into a collective portrait of passion, confrontation, and survival.

The show’s themes are self-determination, artistic courage, and the refusal to let suffering erase identity. It treats love as both a source of connection and conflict, while presenting art as a way to confront pain, mortality, and political change.

show: Gloria - Il Musical, the Italian jukebox musical comedy built on the songs of Umberto Tozzi
synopsis:
Gloria is a gifted, irrepressibly energetic young woman whose greatest ambition is to become a successful singer. Determined to live by the pull of her heart and the force of music, she turns every opportunity into a performance and wins people over with her enthusiasm, warmth, and refusal to settle for an ordinary life. Yet the road toward the spotlight proves far less simple than she imagines. As Gloria pursues her break, her aspirations collide with painful tensions at home, where family expectations and personal loyalties challenge the choices she must make. At the same time, romance opens the possibility of emotional fulfilment, but love also exposes her to disappointment and difficult compromises. New friendships offer encouragement and unexpected moments of joy, while betrayals and concealed schemes threaten both her confidence and her future. Gloria must decide whom she can trust, what she is willing to sacrifice, and whether success is worth achieving if it means losing control of her own voice and identity. Through setbacks, conflicts, and hard-won revelations, she discovers that talent alone cannot carry her forward: she must face the people and pressures seeking to define her life for her. By holding onto her passion while learning from heartbreak and disillusionment, Gloria transforms adversity into resolve. Her journey ultimately carries her from restless longing and uncertainty toward the success she has dreamed of—on terms that are truly her own.

The musical explores the courage required to pursue an artistic dream when family, love, ambition, and betrayal pull in competing directions. At its heart, it celebrates resilience, self-definition, friendship, and the belief that a person’s voice can survive both failure and compromise.

show: Il ragazzo dai pantaloni rosa - Il Musical, the 2026 Teatro Sistina STAGE jukebox musical adapted by Massimo Romeo Piparo and Roberto Proia (the stage version, not the 2024 film)
synopsis:
Andrea, imagined as the adult he might have become, looks back on his final year of middle school and the fragile hope with which he tries to find his place among his classmates. Eager to be accepted, he offers to help Christian, an older repeat student with a feared reputation and a powerful hold over the school’s social order. Andrea’s closest companion is Sara—more mature than her peers and secretly in love with Christian—who becomes his confidante as friendship, longing, and insecurity begin to overlap. At home, his parents’ separation leaves Andrea worried for himself and for his younger brother Daniele, making Christian’s apparent attention feel like a refuge. Instead, Christian turns Andrea’s trust into ammunition, exposing him to ridicule before their classmates. Professor Gioli, Andrea’s music teacher, is one of the few adults to recognise his poetic and musical gifts, urging him to endure until the move to liceo.

For a while, the new school offers relief: Christian is elsewhere, and Andrea and Sara find a calmer rhythm. But Christian soon arrives at their liceo, presenting himself as changed. When Andrea receives a pair of red trousers that turn pink in the wash, he chooses to wear them to school—a small, personal act that marks him out for renewed mockery. His declaration of love to Sara on Valentine’s Day ends in rejection, and his hurtful response drives her away. Christian and his group then lure Andrea into a supposed school party, persuading him to dress as a prostitute for a social-media video; he arrives alone, humiliated and publicly exposed. On his birthday, after reconciling with Sara and sharing time with his reunited family and Professor Gioli at a luna park, Andrea walks away from the others and steps off the ride of his life.

The musical confronts bullying, cyberbullying, isolation, and the devastating cost of treating difference as a target. It also insists on the importance of empathy, listening to unspoken distress, and actively choosing solidarity rather than remaining a bystander.

show: LUPIN - Il Musical by Compagnia della Corona, original music by Paola Magnanini, book and direction by Salvatore Sito
synopsis:
A glittering adventure begins aboard the Orient Express as it races from Paris to Istanbul. A priceless jewel, the Tulip of Ahmed III, has vanished from its supposedly impregnable safe, and the daring theft signals the return of Lupin, the elusive gentleman thief whose charm, disguises, and audacity make him almost impossible to catch. Yet this is no simple robbery. The stolen tulip is tied to Isabelle, a kind-hearted young orphan in Paris, and Lupin’s interest in her soon proves more personal than strategic. He courts her with a delicate tulip offered day after day, gradually winning her trust while concealing the dangerous world in which he moves.

Isabelle works in a chocolate factory, a place that ought to promise warmth and sweetness but instead feels bleak, oppressive, and full of unspoken threats. Behind its grey façade lie secrets, covert schemes, and forces willing to exploit those with little power or protection. As Lupin follows the trail connecting Isabelle, the factory, and the stolen jewel, the train journey becomes a moving arena for deception, shifting identities, and unexpected alliances. Lupin must stay ahead of those pursuing him while deciding whether his greatest skill—his ability to disappear behind another face—can coexist with the honest affection he feels for Isabelle. Clues emerge, motives collide, and the conspiracy surrounding the factory steadily reveals itself as the Orient Express draws closer to Istanbul. By the journey’s end, what seemed to be an extravagant theft has become part of a larger attempt to expose wrongdoing, protect Isabelle, and determine whether Lupin can choose a future beyond the legend he has created.

The musical explores the tension between appearance and truth: masks, luxury, and elaborate crimes conceal both corruption and genuine longing. At its heart, it is a story of hope, justice, love, and the possibility that even a master of escape may find someone worth staying for.

show: Maradona El Diego - Opera Musical, the Italian original musical with music by Marco Frisina and book by Gianmario Pagano
synopsis:
A boy runs toward a ball with the fierce certainty that it can carry him out of the dust and toward an impossible dream. Diego Armando Maradona’s journey begins in youth, where hunger for redemption, natural brilliance, and the sacrifices demanded by ambition shape both the person and the future legend. As his gift propels him forward, triumph becomes inseparable from the pressure of being watched, judged, claimed, and celebrated by forces far larger than himself.

The story traces Diego’s ascent not as a conventional catalogue of matches and trophies, but as an emotional passage through desire, struggle, devotion, and vulnerability. He becomes a figure of extraordinary charisma and unrepeatable talent, yet the same world that raises him toward glory also scrutinizes his every weakness. The public, the media, and power close in around a man loved by the people while repeatedly placed on trial in the court of opinion. His victories bring exhilaration and a sense of collective belonging, especially in Napoli, where the energy of the stadium and the affection of an entire city turn sporting achievement into something almost sacred.

Alongside Diego’s path stands San Gennaro: alive, ironic, and profound rather than a distant icon. He watches over and accompanies Diego, giving the tale a spiritual, intimate counterpoint as fame, solitude, struggle, and human frailty collide. Diego’s fall does not erase the dream that began in childhood; instead, it reveals the cost of carrying a legend’s weight in a vulnerable human body. Through setbacks and renewal, he continues to search for dignity beneath the image imposed upon him.

The show centres on dreams born in hardship, the longing to rise, and the resilience required after collapse. It treats glory and failure as inseparable parts of a life shaped by talent, love, faith, judgment, and the enduring need to be seen as human.

show: Michelangelo da Caravaggio - A Rebel Rock Musical, the Italian rock musical about the painter Caravaggio
synopsis:
In seventeenth-century Rome, Michelangelo Merisi—known as Caravaggio—arrives as a volatile young painter determined to see the world as it is rather than as the powerful insist it should be. Amid the grandeur and corruption of Papal Rome, he rejects polished religious convention and finds his models among the city’s poor, labourers, prostitutes, and outcasts. His canvases turn their weathered faces, pain, desire, and dignity into saints and Madonnas, creating images of the divine rooted in ordinary human suffering. The startling honesty of his art wins him patrons, including Cardinal Del Monte and Marchesa Costanza Colonna, but also provokes resentment from figures such as the painter Giovanni Baglione, whose hostility grows as Caravaggio’s reputation rises.

Caravaggio’s private life is as combustible as his paintings. He is bound to Maddalena “Lena” Antognetti and to Anna “Annuccia” Bianchini, while his uncompromising temperament repeatedly draws him into quarrels, rivalries, and violence. In taverns, streets, studios, and aristocratic rooms, Rome becomes a maze of desire, jealousy, patronage, surveillance, and concealed motives. Don Fernando, the Seville art dealer who recounts the painter’s story, frames the telling, while Caravaggio’s conflict with Ranuccio Tomassoni drives the story toward its most dangerous turning point. His refusal to compromise—either in love, honour, or art—leaves him increasingly isolated, even as the force of his vision becomes impossible to ignore.

After violence makes Rome untenable, Caravaggio is forced into flight. Pursued by the consequences of his own actions, he continues his desperate search for safety, forgiveness, and light, while the shadow of death closes around him. The final movement follows a man whose greatest gift and deepest wound are inseparable: his need to reveal truth, whatever it costs.

The musical explores rebellion against hypocrisy, the collision of artistic integrity with political and religious power, and the uneasy bond between beauty and suffering. Above all, it presents Caravaggio’s lifelong struggle to find light within a world governed by darkness.

show: Peter Pan il Musical, the Italian musical with music by Edoardo Bennato, directed by Maurizio Colombi
synopsis:
In London’s Kensington Gardens, a Storyteller invites children to enter a world where imagination can become real. Among them is Peter Pan, the boy who refuses to grow up. One night, while searching for his lost shadow, Peter arrives at the Darling family home and meets Wendy, John, and Michael. Captivated by Wendy’s stories and by the promise of adventure, Peter teaches the three children to fly. Guided by Tinker Bell’s fairy dust, they soar away to Neverland.

On the island, Wendy, John, and Michael encounter Peter’s unruly companions, the Lost Boys, as well as Tiger Lily and her people, mermaids, and the pirate crew led by Captain Hook. Hook is haunted by the ticking Crocodile that once took his hand and now stalks him relentlessly. Determined to take revenge on Peter, Hook and his first mate, Smee, devise a series of traps. The rivalry brings danger to everyone around Peter, while Wendy tries to create warmth and order among the Lost Boys by telling stories and caring for them.

As the children begin to miss home, Hook’s plans grow more ruthless. He captures Wendy, John, Michael, and the Lost Boys, then secretly leaves poisoned medicine for the sleeping Peter. Tinker Bell discovers the trap and risks her own life to save him. Peter awakens in time to pursue the pirates to their ship, where he frees his friends and confronts Hook in a final swordfight. Peter defeats the captain, who is driven toward the waiting Crocodile, and peace returns to Neverland. Wendy and her brothers then fly back to London, while Peter remains behind with the Lost Boys and Tinker Bell.

The musical explores the freedom and exhilaration of childhood imagination, set against the fear of growing older and leaving fantasy behind. It also values friendship, courage, loyalty, and the comfort of home.

show: Raffaella il Musical, the Italian biographical musical about Raffaella Carrà, written and directed by Luciano Cannito, produced by Viola Produzioni
synopsis:
A shy young Raffaella Pelloni arrives in Roma from Bellaria, carrying the discipline of classical dance and a fierce, private hope of reaching the stage. Her first steps are not easy: training, auditions and disappointment test her resolve, while Iris and her cousin Nadia remain part of the intimate world behind the ambition. Dance opens a door to cinema, but the young performer is still searching for the place where her personality—direct, playful, determined and unlike anyone else’s—can fully emerge.

That place proves to be television. As Raffaella begins to work with Giovanni Salvi, the demanding world of live entertainment calls for more than technique: she must learn to command the camera, face professional uncertainty and turn vulnerability into an unmistakable stage presence. Along the way, Alessandro offers friendship and support, while Gianni Boncompagni becomes both her first great love and a formative artistic partner. Their relationship intertwines affection, creative discovery and the pressures of a career accelerating before Raffaella has fully found her public voice.

Through rehearsals, broadcasts, dances and songs, Raffaella transforms from a reserved young dancer into a performer able to make an entire audience feel personally invited into the celebration. The story traces the difficult early years, the passage through film and television, and the succession of breakthroughs that lead to Canzonissima. Each professional triumph demands courage: to be visible, to take risks, to claim artistic freedom and to refuse the limits others might place on a woman in the public eye. By the time the spotlight truly belongs to her, Raffaella has forged the exuberant, open-hearted persona that will carry her beyond the boundaries of her beginnings.

At its heart, the show is about perseverance, self-invention and the freedom to express oneself without apology. It celebrates how discipline, love, friendship and creative daring can turn a young artist’s uncertain dream into a shared burst of joy.

show: Win for life, the Italian musical comedy created by the group Oblivion and directed by Giorgio Gallione
synopsis:
When a stranger rings Mila’s doorbell with an unbelievable offer—€8,000 every day for the rest of her life—she accepts. The windfall comes with one uncompromising condition: she must never reveal the money’s existence to anyone. If she does, every euro must be returned. Mila, an Eastern European domestic worker whose ordinary life has offered little security, suddenly finds herself at the centre of a private fortune so immense that it becomes almost impossible to conceal. Each new delivery of cash brings not relief but a fresh practical and moral problem: where can she put it, how can she explain the changes in her life, and how long can she maintain a lie among the people closest to her?

At home, her secret is tested by a feckless husband absorbed in grand, impractical schemes, a yoga-minded daughter whose apparent spirituality does not stop her from watching the family finances, and an irascible elderly relative who communicates largely through blunt outbursts. Mila also carries a private romantic obsession with historian Alessandro Barbero and his Robin Hood podcasts, a fantasy that sits oddly beside the increasingly dangerous reality around her. Her efforts to keep the bargain hidden draw her into a frantic web of misunderstandings, suspicion, and escalating deception. A loan-shark drug trafficker, a mysterious masked man who arrives with mountains of money, and the shadowy agents of an ancient brotherhood turn the household crisis into an international intrigue. Meanwhile, a chorus and three mariachi musicians repeatedly break into the action, commenting on events and trying—often inconveniently—to keep the story on course. As secrets multiply and the pressure mounts, Mila must decide what she is prepared to sacrifice to preserve the prize that was supposed to transform her life.

The musical explores the seduction and burden of sudden wealth: money promises freedom, yet its secrecy isolates Mila from the people around her. Beneath the farce, it asks whether a life built on concealment, suspicion, and compromise can truly count as winning.

show: Saturnin, the new Czech original musical at Divadlo Hybernia with music by Roman Říčař, adapted and directed by Tomáš Dianiška, after Zdeněk Jirotka's novel
synopsis:
A young man named Jirotka lives a quiet, orderly life in Prague until his newly engaged valet, Saturnin, begins to manage the household according to his own eccentric principles. Impeccably polite yet impossible to restrain, Saturnin repeatedly turns ordinary social situations into carefully engineered chaos. His interventions unsettle Jirotka’s habits, disrupt the expectations of visiting relatives, and create room for the romance between Jirotka and Barbora to move forward. Rather than obeying convention, Saturnin treats it as material for a joke: with perfect composure, he manipulates arrangements, conversations, and coincidences so that people reveal who they really are.

The household is soon crowded with contrasting personalities. Tetička Kateřina arrives armed with an inexhaustible supply of solemn proverbs and a firm belief that every difficulty can be governed by a suitably moral saying. Her son Milouš, pampered and self-important, becomes an especially tempting target for Saturnin’s quiet mischief. Dědeček brings warmth, adventurous imagination, and a taste for stories that make daily life seem far more dangerous and exciting than it is, while Doktor Vlach offers a dry, observant counterpoint to the family’s escalating absurdity. As the group is drawn away from the city into increasingly comic predicaments, Saturnin keeps appearing to anticipate every obstacle—and to make it worse before making it better.

Jirotka must decide whether to cling to the safe, respectable routine expected of him or accept the unpredictable freedom that Saturnin introduces into his life. By the end, the apparent disorder has exposed false dignity, softened rigid family expectations, and helped the hesitant lovers find a clearer path toward one another.

The musical celebrates personal freedom against empty social rules, using farce and romance to show how disruption can become a form of liberation. It also suggests that good manners and rebellion need not be opposites: Saturnin accomplishes his revolution with unfailing elegance.

show: VY NEJSTE ŽENA, PANE!, the Czech original musical comedy written by Karel Janák, directed by Lukáš Burian at Divadlo Radka Brzobohatého
synopsis:
Milan Kokeš and Libor Náramný enter an anonymous dating site hoping to arrange a passionate encounter with a woman. Behind deliberately vague nicknames, each imagines that the unknown person on the other end of the messages is female; their long-awaited date therefore begins with mutual shock when the two men meet face to face. Milan, humiliated and furious at what he sees as a deception, rejects Libor outright and walks away. What could have remained an embarrassing private mishap, however, is seized upon by a lawyer and aspiring politician, Žalobce, who spots an opportunity to turn Milan’s refusal into a public cause campaigned in the name of tolerance.

The incident is brought before a court, where the opposing arguments are staged and repeatedly revisited: is choosing a partner partly on the basis of sex an innocent personal preference, or an act of exclusion demanding public redress? Milan is drawn from an awkward date into an increasingly elaborate legal and political spectacle. Libor’s disappointment becomes evidence in a case that grows far beyond either man’s intentions, while Žalobce uses the proceedings to promote his own cause. Under the gaze of Soudkyně, Přísedící, Obhájkyně and Novinářka, intimate messages, expectations and hurt feelings are transformed into material for judgement, publicity and ideological battle.

The story then widens when that movement wins the election. The movement that rose by promising tolerance acquires the authority to regulate it, and the people who helped create its new order find themselves caught inside it. A farcical misunderstanding consequently develops into a society in which private desire, speech and personal choice are subjected to official scrutiny.

The musical explores how easily a private romantic disappointment can be weaponised in public life. Its central themes are the tension between individual freedom and enforced conformity, the political use of identity and offence, and the danger of power exercised in the name of tolerance.

show: Zlatovláska, the Czech original fairy-tale musical with music by Angelo Michajlov at Hudební divadlo Karlín
synopsis:
Kuchař Jiřík serves at the court of a vain and domineering king. When a mysterious snake is brought to the royal kitchen, the king orders Jiřík to cook it and strictly forbids him to taste it. Jiřík cannot resist tasting it himself. His new gift soon exposes him: he overhears animals speaking and reveals knowledge no ordinary cook should possess. As punishment, the king orders him to travel to a distant realm and bring back the beautiful Zlatovláska, whom the king intends to claim for himself.

On his journey, Jiřík is accompanied by Muška and repeatedly chooses compassion over convenience. He helps mravenci, krkavci and zlatá rybka, earning their loyalty in return. At her father’s court, Zlatovláska is surrounded by her sisters—Černovláska, Rudovláska, Hnědovláska and Plavovláska—and the king sets demanding tasks before the stranger who seeks her hand on another ruler’s behalf. Jiřík’s animal friends repay his kindness by helping him complete the seemingly impossible challenges. As he and Zlatovláska come to know one another, the mission becomes a conflict between obedience and genuine love.

Jiřík returns with Zlatovláska, but the king refuses to accept that her heart belongs to the cook rather than to him. The struggle for Zlatovláska’s future leads to a final reversal in which Jiřík’s steadfastness and the alliances he has formed prevail. The king’s greed turns deadly, but the water of life undoes what his cruelty destroys, and Jiřík and Zlatovláska are united at last. Jiřík ultimately becomes king beside Zlatovláska.

The musical celebrates kindness as a force that creates unexpected allies, while selfish power isolates those who wield it. Its happy resolution affirms loyalty, cooperation, reconciliation and the right to choose love freely.

show: Edudant a Francimor, the Czech family musical at Hudební divadlo Karlín after Karel Poláček's 1933 book
synopsis:
Edudant and Francimor are two wizard brothers: conspicuously handsome in their own estimation, almost twenty years old, and absurdly overdue for first grade. Their mother, the absent-minded sorceress Halabába, has simply neglected to enrol them in school. Once this oversight is discovered, the brothers must finally take their place among much younger classmates. Their swaggering confidence and imperfect grasp of ordinary school life immediately make them outsiders, while the conscientious Ředitel školy tries to keep the new pupils and the whole class on course.

The compulsory school trip to the ruined castle of Růžový patník turns routine education into a headlong magical expedition. Accompanied by their schoolmates, Edudant and Francimor encounter bullying troublemakers, comic dangers, a band of robbers, and a strange town ruled by dogs, where Halabába reappears as Fena Peggy and the schoolmaster becomes Hospodský Brok. The adventure carries them further to the castle of King Růženín, who keeps Princezna Róza and Princezna Růža captive. Along the way, the brothers’ contrasting natures come into focus: Edudant is the warmer and more straightforward of the pair, while Francimor is sharper, more self-assured, and vainly pleased with himself. Yet both prove capable of courage and ingenuity when their companions need them.

Each apparent villain reveals a more complicated private misery: the Loupežník is thwarted by a family unwilling to cooperate in robbery, while King Růženín’s cruelty is rooted less in simple evil than in isolation and unmet emotional needs. By confronting chaos with curiosity, humour, and compassion rather than force alone, the children bring the journey’s tangled conflicts toward resolution.

The musical celebrates friendship, growing up, and the value of meeting an unfamiliar world with empathy. It resists simple good-and-evil divisions, suggesting that mischief and cruelty often conceal loneliness, frustration, or a need to be heard.

show: Čarodějnice Bordelína, the Czech children's musical after the book by Sandra Dražilová Zlámalová, directed by Milan Enčev at Divadlo Radka Brzobohatého
synopsis:
In the quiet forest of Bambručák, life changes abruptly when the young witch Bordelína arrives to make a home for herself. Nothing in this peaceful place pleases her, so she immediately sets about remaking it according to her own unruly taste. Her new house is accompanied by colourful scraps and confetti, and her spells turn everyday life upside down: animals find stinging nettles in place of soft moss in their beds, while children are disturbed at night by Bordelína’s flights on her magical umbrella and the mischief she brings with her. Sova Mudrlice, Veverka Drzečka and Zajíc Cyril, accustomed to the forest’s former calm, cannot understand why their home has been invaded by such chaos. They try to resist the newcomer, but Bordelína’s tricks keep escalating and the forest’s inhabitants become increasingly helpless.

Bordelína has also been taught that a proper witch must be wicked, self-reliant and unwilling to help anyone. Her brother Čaroděj Puchonosor and her cousin Čarodějnice Řachatice reinforce that lesson when they tell her it is time to live alone and practise witchcraft in earnest. Yet their interest in Bordelína is far from affectionate: once she is away, they scheme to take her magical power for themselves. As the conflict in Bambručák grows more tangled, Bordelína must confront both the frightened animals around her and the treachery within her own magical family. Her apparent delight in disorder begins to reveal a more complicated girl—one whose heart may not be as cruel as the role she has been taught to perform.

The musical explores belonging, responsibility and the consequences of treating a shared home as if it belonged to only one person. It also suggests that kindness can emerge when someone questions the harmful identity others have imposed on them.

show: Rebelové, the Czech jukebox musical of 1960s Czech hits at Hudební divadlo Karlín, after Filip Renč's 2001 film
synopsis:
In the summer of 1968, freshly graduated friends Tereza, Bugyna and Julča spend their days in a small town near the border, impatient for romance, music and a future that seems wide open. Their carefree world is disrupted by the arrival of three soldiers—Šimon, Bob and Eman—who have deserted the army and are lying low while they wait for their chance to escape across the border. The men’s plan is audacious: they hope to hide aboard a train carrying timber to West Germany and begin new lives in San Francisco.

Tereza and Šimon are drawn together almost at once, and their intense first love becomes the centre of a summer filled with flirtation, dance and impulsive promises. Around them, Bugyna, Julča, Bob and Eman form their own shifting pairings, while the older generation’s lives add further complications: Tereza’s father finds love with Alžběta, and the watchful Farář and Průvodčí Douša stand at the edge of the young people’s increasingly dangerous adventure. As the escape plan comes closer, private longing begins to collide with political reality.

The would-be emigrants are discovered before they can reach freedom. Šimon is imprisoned, while Tereza leaves the country with her father and Alžběta, separating the lovers just as their relationship has become most profound. The story’s bright, youthful mood is finally overtaken by the August invasion of Czechoslovakia by Warsaw Pact forces, which abruptly ends the illusion that freedom and happiness can simply be chosen.

The show is about young love meeting history at its most unforgiving moment. It contrasts the exhilaration of friendship, rebellion and imagined escape with loss, separation and the sudden end of innocence.

show: Anděl Páně, the Czech original musical comedy with music and lyrics by Ondřej G. Brzobohatý, directed by Martin Čičvák at Hudební divadlo Karlín
synopsis:
Petronel is a restless, accident-prone angel whose place in heaven is suddenly at risk. Given one final chance by Bůh, he must go down to Earth and reform a sinner, proving that he can be useful rather than a continual source of heavenly disorder. His unwanted companion is Uriáš, a sly and malicious devil who appears eager to guide Petronel but instead delights in exploiting every weakness in the angel’s judgment. Together they arrive among human beings, where Petronel is certain that detecting sin and correcting it will be simple.

The earthly world proves far more complicated. Petronel encounters Správce and Klíčnice, figures whose selfishness and intrigues create the practical obstacles of the story. He also meets Dorotka and Hrabě, whose kindness, loyalty, and capacity for love offer a very different picture of humanity. Petronel’s impulsiveness and naïveté repeatedly turn attempted interventions into fresh confusion: his good intentions are easily diverted by Uriáš, and his certainty that he understands right and wrong gives way to painful mistakes. As events become increasingly tangled, the fate of the people around him is bound up with Petronel’s own trial. He must learn to see past appearances, confront manipulation, and accept responsibility for the harm caused by his choices.

In the end, human love, steadfast hope, and help from the heavenly world enable the damage to be set right and expose the injustice behind the plots of Správce and Klíčnice. Petronel succeeds not by acting as a flawless judge of others, but by recognizing his own faults. The sinner he finally manages to reform is Petronel himself, allowing him to return to heaven.

The musical’s central themes are redemption, humility, and the difficult difference between judging people and truly understanding them. It suggests that goodness is expressed through compassion and accountability, while even a fallible angel can change when he learns from love and failure.

show: Močál Story, the Czech musical comedy written and composed by Ivan Mládek, directed by Vilém Dubnička at Hudební divadlo Karlín
synopsis:
When a classmate disappears during a walk in the woods, Stáňa Poláková and Dáša Nováková set out to discover what has happened to her. Their concern soon draws in Komisař Bambula, whose official authority is matched by a conspicuous talent for confusion, and Policista Véna “Rambo”, his equally muddled partner. What might have been a straightforward missing-person case quickly becomes an increasingly absurd expedition away from ordinary logic and into a landscape where every new encounter sends the investigation in an unexpected direction.

Following scraps of information and their own unreliable instincts, the search party ventures toward the bažina, where they meet Jožin z bažin. Rather than bringing the case neatly to a close, this encounter enlarges the mystery and sets the tone for a journey populated by eccentric figures. Linda appears with her own domestic complications, while Jenda Benda crosses the investigators’ path as another unlikely participant in their wandering inquiry. The group also encounters vampires, a mayor, a myslivec, a houbař, a hasič, a listonoška, a ježibaba, and a succession of other strange inhabitants and visitors whose presence turns each clue into another comic detour.

As Bambula and Véna “Rambo” try to impose the procedures of a police investigation on events that refuse to behave sensibly, Stáňa and Dáša continue their own determined search. The missing girl remains the thread connecting the episodes, but the pursuit repeatedly slips into misunderstandings, chance meetings, playful threats, and surreal turns. By moving through the forest, the bažina, and a chain of encounters that are at once suspicious and ridiculous, the characters transform a simple search into a rambling comic adventure in which the route matters as much as the resolution.

The musical’s plot centres on friendship and persistence in the face of confusion. It also celebrates comic disorder: official competence collapses, the unfamiliar becomes ordinary, and an anxious search becomes a cheerful journey through a wildly eccentric world.

show: Kapka medu pro Verunku, the Czech original family musical with libretto by Jan Pixa and Alena Pixová
synopsis:
On a fairy-tale island, the neighboring kingdoms of Zlatovláskov, Popelkov, and Honzovsko have long lived peacefully, trading, helping one another, and sharing a prosperous life. Yet their rulers have grown careless: while enjoying the island’s abundance, they have allowed its natural world to be neglected. A new crisis arrives when Princess Verunka of Zlatovláskov reaches marriageable age. Through poor communication among the royal families, both Princ Mirek of Popelkov and Princ Honza of Honzovsko come to seek her hand. Neither prince can be rejected lightly, since a slight to either kingdom could turn a courtship into a conflict between nations. Verunka, meanwhile, has her own hopes for whom she might marry, and the pressure of the competing arrangements leaves everyone at an impasse.

Watching the humans misuse and undervalue nature, Kapeska—the queen of the forces of nature—decides that the royal households, especially the young men who may one day rule, must be taught a lesson. With the help of fairy-tale beings, she sets a stern test in motion for the royal families, and above all for the princes who will one day rule. The princes, joined by Myslivec Jirka, set out on it. Their journey confronts them with obstacles, dangers, and tasks that reveal the contrast among their temperaments: strength alone will not suffice, cleverness has limits, and fine words mean little without courage, compassion, and a good heart. As the rescuers face the consequences of the older generation’s failures, the rivalry that threatened the island gives way to a deeper understanding of responsibility, friendship, and what worthy leadership requires.

The musical is ultimately about love that cannot be reduced to a political arrangement, and about friendship forged through shared trials. It also frames care for nature as a moral responsibility, insisting that future rulers must treat both one another and their world with greater wisdom.

show: Snowboarďáci, the Czech original musical after Karel Janák's 2004 film, directed by Lukáš Burian at Divadlo Radka Brzobohatého
synopsis:
Rendy and Jáchym head to the snowy resort of Špindlerův Mlýn determined to turn a winter break into a rite of passage. They want to master the slopes, prove themselves among the more experienced snowboarders, and—above all—escape their inexperience in love and sex. Their confidence is largely performance: beneath the bravado, each is anxious about being embarrassed, rejected, or left behind. The boys’ friendship is tested as their efforts to look worldly turn into competition, particularly when Lucka enters their orbit. Both are drawn to her, and the rivalry shifts between comic posturing, genuine attraction, and the uncomfortable recognition that neither can simply treat her as a prize.

Around them, the crowded resort supplies temptations, misunderstandings, and escalating mishaps. Panter embodies the intimidating, seemingly effortless cool the boys wish they possessed, while Milan and the other holidaymakers add pressure to the boys’ attempts to belong. A Nymfomanka pursues her own direct desires, making Rendy and Jáchym confront the gap between their fantasies and the awkward reality of intimacy. Meanwhile, Marta’s feelings for Rendy introduce a quieter, more sincere possibility: unlike the boys’ casual boasts and competitive flirting, she wants to be seen and taken seriously. Her presence forces Rendy to choose between chasing status and acknowledging someone who genuinely cares for him.

The holiday’s comic crises unfold amid snowboarding bravado, romantic confusion, and the boys’ repeated attempts to control situations they barely understand. As confrontations and disappointments strip away their poses, Rendy and Jáchym must decide what matters more: winning Lucka’s attention, impressing one another and the people around them, or preserving their friendship. The mountains become a testing ground where their fantasies of adulthood collide with its emotional consequences.

The show explores adolescence as a volatile mix of friendship, desire, insecurity, and the urge to appear more grown-up than one feels. It contrasts competitive conquest with honest affection, suggesting that maturity begins when bravado gives way to responsibility for other people’s feelings.

show: A dzsungel könyve, the Hungarian musical with music by Dés László, lyrics by Geszti Péter and book by Békés Pál, premiered 1996 at Pesti Színház
synopsis:
In a village ruled by fear and ritual, Sir Kán attacks Maugli’s family, killing his father and driving the child into the jungle. There Akela, leader of the szioni wolf pack, proposes that the wolves take him in. Sir Kán demands the boy for himself, but the DzsTK requires two sponsors for adoption: Balu, teacher of the Law, and Bagira, the black panther, stand for Maugli, while Bagira seals the decision with an ox. Maugli grows up among the wolves, taught by Balu and protected by Bagira, yet his curiosity repeatedly leads him beyond the rules. The monkeys abduct him and make him their leader, only to turn on him; Ká subdues them and nearly devours Maugli before Balu and Bagira intervene. Later, Maugli falls into Kobra’s treasure pit. He accepts an ankus out of pity, then watches humans kill one another for it, learning why Bagira fears their greed.

When the ageing Akela fails a hunting trial, Sir Kán exploits the wolves’ unrest and claims the leadership. Bagira sends Maugli to fetch the red flower—fire—from the human settlement. Maugli returns with torches, saves Akela, and drives Sir Kán away, but the pack has already fractured. As Balu leaves to die, Maugli resolves to defeat Sir Kán and then seek a place among humans. In the village, Túna teaches him language and helps the women welcome him, while Buldeó and the other men distrust him. Maugli confronts Sir Kán in the jungle, kills him, and takes his skin, but finds the wolf pack dispersed. Back in the village, Buldeó accuses him of witchcraft. Maugli breaks Buldeó’s gun yet refuses revenge; instead, he gives Sir Kán’s skin to free Túna, choosing a future with her even as he recognises that he belongs fully to neither world.

The musical explores belonging, exclusion, and the difficult passage from childhood into adulthood. It sets loyalty, compassion, and chosen family against fear, violence, greed, and the temptation to define others as strangers.

show: A Padlás, the Hungarian musical with music by Presser Gábor, lyrics by Sztevanovity Dusán and book by Horváth Péter, premiered 1988 at Vígszínház
synopsis:
In a cluttered Budapest attic perched “between heaven and earth,” Rádiós, an inventive cyberneticist, works on Robinson, his sensitive supercomputer, while Süni, the violin-studying girl next door, quietly loves him. The attic is visited by four long-wandering spirits—Herceg, Kölyök, Lámpás and the silent giant Meglökő—who believe it is the place where Révész will collect them and carry them to the planet of the “örökre szépek.” Mamóka, the warm-hearted old woman of the house, can see the spirits and welcomes them as if they were family; the suspicious Témüller cannot see them and merely looks for grounds to harass Rádiós.

Their refuge is endangered when Barrabás B. Barrabás, a wanted gangster, breaks in through the roof. He assaults Rádiós, escapes, and is shot while fleeing. Yet the body that returns is inhabited by Révész, who has secretly assumed Barrabás’s form in order to experience human life. Rádiós and Süni hide him when Detektív and Üteg arrive, hunting the criminal, while Témüller tries to turn every confusion into an accusation. Révész promises that at dawn he will leave the borrowed body and take the four spirits onward, but the authorities surround the building, and the attic itself comes under threat.

As police helicopters move to destroy the roof, Süni risks herself to repair Robinson’s antenna. Rádiós uses the machine to summon a sudden snowstorm, driving the helicopters away. The spirits finally depart with Révész, leaving Süni the Varázskönyv and prompting Rádiós to recognize his love for her. Then Üteg reveals that Barrabás left a timed bomb behind. With Süni refusing to abandon him, Rádiós follows the Varázskönyv’s guidance and disables it. Barrabás’s actual body is found, Témüller is arrested for his false accusations, and the reformed spirit of Barrabás emerges seeking help.

The musical explores remembrance as a force that preserves people, places and love beyond loss. It sets kindness, imagination and solidarity against fear, bureaucracy and cruelty, while making the attic a fragile sanctuary where the living learn to see one another clearly.

show: Macskafogó, the Hungarian musical at József Attila Színház after Béla Ternovszky's 1986 Hungarian animated film
synopsis:
In the year M. M. u. 80, the mouse population of Planet X faces extinction under the rule of the cats. The feline criminal world, led by the feared Mr. Fritz Teufel and supported by figures including Safranek and Lusta Dick, has turned the conflict into an organised campaign of terror. The mouse authorities of Intermouse have exhausted their ordinary options, so they turn to their long-retired master agent, Nick Grabowski. Nick is the mice’s last credible hope: he must travel to Pokió and retrieve the revolutionary invention of Fushimishi professzor, a device known as the Macskafogó, which may finally give the mice a means to resist their enemies.

The mission unfolds as a high-stakes espionage adventure, with Nick moving through a world of gangsters, spies, compromised institutions, and ever-present cat surveillance. While Intermouse attempts to protect the operation, the cats learn enough to mobilise their own network against him. Teufel’s side seeks to stop the invention before it can reach the threatened mouse community, using intimidation, deception, pursuit, and the allure of betrayal. Along Nick’s route, allies and adversaries emerge in shifting combinations: Bob Poliakoff, Edlington, Giovanni Gatto, Cicus, Billy, Buddy, Cookie, Pissy, Chino san, Nero von Schwarz, and Maxipotzac all belong to the unstable, comic, and dangerous international struggle surrounding the mission.

As the pursuit closes in, Nick must rely on his old instincts, nerve, and refusal to abandon a cause that others have almost given up for lost. The central question is whether he can return from Pokió with Fushimishi professzor’s invention in time—and whether the Macskafogó can truly be brought to life before the cats complete their domination of Planet X.

The show centres on courage under pressure, collective survival, and the possibility that ingenuity can overturn apparently absolute power. Beneath its comic crime-and-spy adventure, it argues that solidarity and persistence matter most when fear makes resistance seem impossible.

show: Légy jó mindhalálig, the Hungarian musical with music by Kocsák Tibor and book by Miklós Tibor, after Zsigmond Móricz's novel
synopsis:
In Debrecen, the sensitive, homesick Nyilas Misi enters the Kollégium carrying the memory of his family and a fierce determination to study diligently. Life among the boys is harsher than he expects: when a food parcel arrives from home, his fellow pupils consume not only its contents but even his boot polish, exposing the casual cruelty beneath their camaraderie. Yet Misi finds moments of kindness. Valkay tanár úr secures him a tutoring post with the Doroghy family, and Misi also reads aloud to the blind Pósalaky úr, hoping that his earnings can ease his parents’ poverty. At the Doroghy household, he is drawn to Bella kisasszony, whose affection is fixed instead on the reckless Török János.

The adult world that Misi longs to join proves even more treacherous. Pósalaky úr entrusts him with a lutriszelvény, and Misi proudly carries it with him. Török János notices the ticket, takes it, and runs away with Bella kisasszony. Misi believes he has merely lost it, but the ticket is a winner, and suspicion swiftly turns against the bewildered schoolboy. When a ten-forint note planted by Török János is found in Misi’s pocket, the Kollégium’s disciplinary authorities accuse him of embezzlement. Questioned and humiliated, Misi cannot make the adults understand the plain truth of his innocence. Even when the theft is ultimately uncovered and he is cleared, vindication cannot undo the damage: illness, shame, and the collapse of his trust leave him emotionally exhausted. He says farewell to Debrecen and resolves never to return as its pupil.

The musical traces a child’s painful encounter with injustice, class pressure, and adult hypocrisy. It also affirms that Misi’s wounded compassion and desire to teach humanity to be good can survive betrayal and humiliation.

show: MADE IN HUNGÁRIA, the Hungarian rock jukebox musical built on Fenyő Miklós's songs
synopsis:
In early-1960s Budapest, Ricky returns with his family to Angyalföld after years in America, bringing a head full of rock and roll, a Hawaiian shirt, and the conviction that music can make the grey streets feel like another world. He reunites with Rudi, Csipu, Tripolisz and Kis Nyírő, and throws himself into turning their local group into a band with the nerve, sound and style to shake up the neighbourhood. Ricky’s imported swagger initially makes him an object of fascination, but it also makes him an outsider in a place governed by suspicion, official taste and everyday compromises.

His return is complicated by Vera, the girl he once loved. In Ricky’s absence, Vera has become involved with Röné, the self-assured “csókkirály” and guitarist whose charm masks a ruthless streak. The rivalry between Ricky and Röné becomes both romantic and musical: each wants Vera’s loyalty, the crowd’s attention and the right to define what youth culture in Angyalföld will sound like. Around them, Marina, Duci Juci, Sampon and the members of Figaro intensify the contests, jealousies, flirtations and public confrontations that surround the bands.

As rehearsals, dances and local appearances build toward a decisive public performance, Ricky must learn that American gestures alone cannot win either the audience or Vera. The group’s bid to make itself heard runs into the pressure represented by Bigali elvtárs and the watchful machinery of authority, while the young people negotiate friendship, family expectations, romantic betrayal and the risk of standing out. By transforming their own experience into loud, exuberant performance, Ricky and his friends turn a fight for recognition into a communal celebration in which private heartbreak and public rebellion collide.

The musical is about the liberating force of music, the hunger for self-expression, and the attempt to create colour and freedom within a restrictive world. It also explores first love, rivalry, loyalty and the difficult process of finding an authentic voice rather than merely copying a dream.

show: A meseautó, the Hungarian musical comedy (zenés vígjáték) produced by Veres 1 Színház, after the 1934 Hungarian film Meseautó
synopsis:
Szűcs János, the impeccably self-assured managing director of the Központi bank, plans to escape Budapest for a month of solitude—away from work, society, and, above all, women. Before leaving, he indulges himself by buying a magnificent blue Horch 780 cabriolet from Péterffy Tamás’s automobile salon. There he notices Kovács Vera, a young shorthand typist from a modest budai confectioner’s family, who has come simply to admire the car. Vera is captivated by the Horch, and Szűcs János is captivated by Vera; his carefully arranged holiday immediately becomes a pursuit.

Determined to find out whether Vera could care for him rather than his position and wealth, Szűcs János hides his identity and appears as an ordinary chauffeur. A web of comic misunderstandings follows: Vera must navigate the attentions of a man she believes to be merely a driver, while the powerful bank director seems to vanish behind a disguise. The scheme draws in Szűcs János’s lovesick secretary, Anna kisasszony; the petty and officious Halmos Aladár; the resourceful Stux; and Péterffy Tamás, whose salon becomes the starting point for the romantic masquerade. Meanwhile, Vera’s excitable family—Kovács Sándor, Etel, and Pityu—reacts to the unexpected prospect that their daughter may be moving in very different social circles.

As identities are confused, status is performed, and romantic pride gets in the way, Vera discovers that the apparently humble chauffeur is not who he claims to be. Hurt by the deception, she rejects Szűcs János just as he is ready to abandon the game. Amid a mistaken dinner arrangement and an escalating orfeum commotion involving J. B., the farce finally unravels. Szűcs János must reveal himself honestly and prove that his feelings for Vera are genuine; only then can the two overcome the gulf between their worlds and choose each other.

At its heart, the show celebrates love that tests the distance between wealth and ordinary life, glamour and sincerity. Its comic disguises and reversals suggest that happiness begins only when people stop treating each other as roles and recognize one another truthfully.

show: Nikola Tesla - Végtelen energia, the Hungarian original musical with book by Egressy Zoltán, premiered 2020 in Pomáz
synopsis:
Nikola Tesla bends over the dust of the Városliget, sketching with a stick the principle of the alternating-current motor as an idea he can already see whole in his mind. Beside him stands his closest friend, Szigeti Antal, whose loyalty anchors the restless young engineer during his years in Magyarország. From the memories of Smiljan and the influence of Duka Tesla, Nikola’s journey carries him through Prága, Budapest and Párizs, where ambition, solitude and an almost obsessive faith in invention shape his path.

In Budapest, work at the Puskás Tivadar Telefontársaság offers Nikola a first professional foothold, while his friendships and encounters—especially with Szigeti Antal and Szigeti Adél—expose the personal cost of a mind permanently drawn toward the next impossible discovery. He eventually crosses the Atlantic to New York, convinced that America will supply the means to turn his visions into reality. Instead, he enters a harsh contest of power, money and competing electrical systems. Thomas Alva Edison becomes the formidable rival whose commercial pragmatism clashes with Nikola’s uncompromising imagination.

Nikola’s ideas find a more sympathetic champion in George Westinghouse, and the struggle over electricity grows into a public battle whose stakes reach far beyond laboratories and patents. Amid the dazzling spectacle of the Chicagói Világkiállítás, Nikola’s alternating current demonstrates its potential to transform modern life. The triumph leads toward the Niagara-vízesés, where the force of nature is harnessed on an unprecedented scale—bringing Nikola closer to the childhood dream that has driven him from one country, one loss and one experiment to the next. Yet achievement does not resolve the loneliness of the visionary, whose extraordinary gifts continually set him apart from the people around him.

The musical centres on imagination confronting commercial power, and on the price of pursuing an idea others cannot yet understand. It also treats electricity as both a technological force and a metaphor for human connection, ambition and the desire to bring light into the world.

show: A TRÓN, the new Hungarian original musical about Hunyadi Mátyás, world premiere at Erkel Színház in Budapest
synopsis:
At Nándorfehérvár, the Hunyadi family’s hard-won victory gives way almost at once to mourning when Hunyadi János dies, leaving his sons László and Mátyás exposed in a court where loyalty shifts with the prospect of power. The young king, Ladislaus (V. László), sits uneasily on the throne, vulnerable to the influence of ambitious figures around him, including Cillei Ulrik and Garai László. As the Hunyadis’ standing makes them appear dangerous to the crown, political manoeuvres harden into a conspiracy against the family.

Hunyadi László becomes the immediate target. His fate devastates Szilágyi Erzsébet and forces Mátyás, still the younger brother, to confront a world in which rank offers no safety and justice can be manipulated by those who hold authority. Garai Anna brings a more intimate current into the struggle, while Petrus stands beside Mátyás as companion and ally amid betrayal, pursuit, and courtly intrigue. Zofia, Jan Giskra, Habsburg III. Frigyes, and Podjebrád Kunigunda each become part of the larger contest over who will control Hungary’s future.

With Mátyás now a potential rival, Ladislaus attempts to remove him from the centre of power, taking him to Prague rather than allowing him to become a rallying point at home. Yet exile does not erase Mátyás’s claim or the memory of what has been done to his family. The conflict turns on his return, as private grief becomes public purpose and a frightened young man is compelled to choose whether to submit to events or shape them. The story culminates in Mátyás’s homecoming and ascent to the throne, transforming the survivor of a shattered household into a king.

The musical’s central themes are the cost of power, the fragility of justice, and the way political violence reaches into family life. It also asks whether fate governs a person’s path, or whether decisive action can reclaim it.

show: Mindig itt leszünk... Mohács 500, the Hungarian rock musical by Szomor György, world premiere 2026 in Mohács, produced by Budapesti Operettszínház
synopsis:
Mindig itt leszünk... Mohács 500 follows II. Lajos as the young king of Hungary comes of age beneath the shadow of an approaching Ottoman invasion. He inherits a realm burdened by division, political rivalry and the knowledge that the forces gathering against it are vastly stronger. Yet, rather than retreating from his responsibility, Lajos resolves to stand with his country. His private life and public duty are bound together through his relationship with Habsburg Mária, whose love for the king is tested by the escalating crisis and by the painful recognition that devotion cannot shield them from history.

Around the royal couple, the conflicting currents of the age intensify. II. Ulászló represents the legacy left to his son; Szapolyai János embodies the internal struggles over authority and the country’s future; and Tomori Pál becomes a figure of military resolve as Hungary prepares to defend itself. Their intersecting ambitions, loyalties and warnings reveal a nation attempting to find unity when time is already running out. The story moves toward Mohács, where Lajos and those who follow him confront not only an enemy army but also the consequences of political fracture, delayed decisions and the unbearable demands placed on individuals in moments of national catastrophe.

The battle brings loss rather than triumph: Mohács falls, Lajos’s fate is sealed, and a defining defeat enters Hungary’s memory. But the ending refuses to treat defeat as disappearance. Through those who remain and through the endurance of collective memory, the story affirms that a people can survive even its darkest historical rupture.

The musical’s central themes are love under pressure, duty in the face of overwhelming odds, sacrifice, and national endurance. It frames Mohács as both a tragedy and a declaration that loss cannot erase identity or hope.

show: Hogyan tudnék élni nélküled?, the Hungarian jukebox musical built on Demjén Ferenc's songs, staged at Erkel Színház
synopsis:
In the present day, Major Lili is lonely and keeps telling herself that she is fine that way. While clearing out the family home with her siblings, Major Döme and Major Luca, she finds a box of old letters and Eszter’s diary. The pages reveal a hidden chapter in her mother’s youth, carrying the story back to a summer at Balaton in the 1990s. There, the young Eszter arrives for a holiday with her friends Kata and Betti. A small mishap on the beach brings them into contact with Gergő and his friends Gábor and Csabi, members of the band Kuplung.

Eszter and Gergő are immediately drawn to one another. Their encounters amid swimming, dancing, rehearsals, and long summer evenings turn a carefree holiday into an intense first love. Yet Eszter is tied to Major Márton, the dependable man expected to be her future, while Gergő represents a riskier life shaped by music, freedom, and emotional honesty. As the relationship becomes impossible to dismiss as a passing flirtation, Eszter must confront the difference between the life arranged around her and the one she might choose for herself. The consequences of that choice do not remain in the past: the discovery of the diary forces Lili and her siblings to reconsider what they believed about Eszter, Gergő, their family, and the unfinished emotions that have crossed generations.

The musical moves between the young lovers’ Balaton summer and the present-day reckoning, allowing the older Eszter and Gergő to face the memories their younger selves created. For Lili, uncovering the truth becomes part of learning that grief need not mean remaining faithful to pain forever.

At its heart, the show explores love as both a joyful beginning and a lasting responsibility, asking whether people can truly let go of the lives they once imagined. It also links personal memory to healing: confronting an inherited past helps the younger generation find the courage to trust, love, and begin again.

show: Zrínyi 1566, the Hungarian historical musical written by Moravetz Levente with music by Balásy Szabolcs, Horváth Krisztián and Papp Zoltán, premiered 2009 in Szigetvár
synopsis:
On 7 September 1566, the siege of Szigetvár is ending in ruin. Only three defenders remain alive, among them Cserenkó Ferenc, chamberlain to Zrínyi Miklós. In the aftermath, Cserenkó will set down what is presented as the true account of the siege—but his record leaves crucial events unspoken, especially the fate of the women whom Zrínyi Miklós could not evacuate to his estate at Csáktornya and who nevertheless do not fall into enemy hands. The musical returns to those silences within the fortress: while the Ottoman forces under Szokoli Mehmed and their commanders, including Perván and Ali, tighten their grip around Szigetvár, Zrínyi and his exhausted Magyar and horvát defenders confront the certainty that relief will not arrive. Within the castle, Rosenberg Éva, Anna, Kata, Borbála and Csenge stand alongside the soldiers, their private attachments and fears becoming inseparable from the community’s struggle to retain dignity amid siege, hunger and approaching death. Zrínyi’s son György also embodies the continuity endangered by the catastrophe. Officers such as Novák János, Kecskés György, Dandó Ferenc, Radován Jakab, Gerecs Bartolus and Orsits István must decide how long courage can hold when survival is no longer a realistic outcome. On the opposing side, the besiegers are not merely a distant army but a force with its own hierarchy, desires and human faces, including Lahib and Lulla. As Szigetvár falls, Cserenkó survives to carry the story forward—yet the ending insists that official remembrance cannot fully contain the sacrifices, choices and disappearances of those trapped within the walls.

The musical’s central themes are steadfastness under overwhelming pressure, loyalty to one’s community, and the cost borne by both fighters and civilians. It also questions who gets remembered in history, and what painful truths may remain concealed even in an eyewitness account.

show: Elvált nők klubja, the Hungarian musical comedy produced by Liliom Produkció, after Olivia Goldsmith's novel
synopsis:
In 1969, four inseparable graduates—Xintia, Elise, Brenda and Annie—promise one another lifelong friendship. Time, marriage and diverging ambitions gradually scatter them, until Xintia’s suicide brings the survivors back together. At her funeral, Elise, Brenda and Annie discover not only how much they have lost by growing apart, but also how similarly their lives have unravelled: each has been discarded by her husband in favour of a younger woman, and each has been left emotionally wounded and financially exposed.

Their reunion begins in grief and humiliation, but it soon develops into a pact of mutual support. Annie has been trapped in a marriage that has drained her confidence; Brenda has endured the consequences of a husband’s betrayals; and Elise, outwardly glamorous, finds that status and appearance have not protected her from loneliness or rejection. Rather than accepting the role of defeated “first wives,” the three women compare notes, rediscover their resourcefulness and begin to understand how much labour, loyalty and insight they once contributed to their husbands’ success.

The women transform their anger into a coordinated campaign against their ex-husbands. Armed with intimate knowledge of the men’s business dealings, weaknesses and vanities, they devise increasingly bold schemes to make them confront the cost of treating their former partners as disposable. The revenge is comic, inventive and pointed, but the real change occurs within the women themselves: old resentments give way to trust, self-pity becomes resolve, and their friendship becomes a source of practical power. What starts as a reckoning with the past becomes an opportunity to rebuild independent lives on their own terms.

At its heart, Elvált nők klubja is about friendship reclaimed after years of separation, and about turning betrayal into solidarity. It celebrates self-respect, female agency and the possibility of beginning again when the life one expected has fallen apart.

show: Carmen, the Frank Wildhorn musical (music Frank Wildhorn, lyrics Jack Murphy, book Norman Allen), world premiere 2008 at the Karlín Musical Theatre in Prague
synopsis:
In a provincial town, police officer José is newly engaged to the devout Katarina, daughter of the Mayor. Their respectable future is unsettled when a travelling circus arrives and its magnetic performer, Carmen, catches José’s attention by giving him a rose. Carmen’s presence excites the town and attracts several powerful, possessive men: the Mayor himself, police captain Zuniga, and knife thrower García. After Carmen wounds a man who harasses her, Zuniga orders José to escort her to the station. On the way, Carmen flirts with him and kisses him, beginning an attraction that draws José away from Katarina and into danger. Carmen warns José about García, yet invites him to the fair; there, Zuniga again presses his unwanted attentions and García insists that Carmen belongs to him. When Zuniga discovers Carmen and José together at a fountain and attempts to take her away, García attacks him. Carmen and José escape, but García uses José’s gun to kill Zuniga, leaving José implicated in the crime.

As the town searches for the supposed murderer, Carmen learns that García was responsible and that he plans revenge against José and anyone José loves. José, tormented by betraying Katarina, wants to clear his name rather than flee with Carmen. García prepares a public trap at the circus, binding Katarina to the “wheel of betrayal” and threatening her life. Carmen chooses to protect the woman who stands between her and José: she warns Katarina in church, then takes Katarina’s place on the wheel during the performance. García admits the murder and hurls a knife at Carmen, but Inmar shoots him before he can strike again. Carmen nevertheless dies from the attack, while Katarina leaves behind the devastation.
